headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

Here’s a quick “cheat‑sheet” you can use to find a short (≤ 2 h) film right on foot from Times Square: | Theater | Approx. walk from Times Square | How to check the runtime | |---------|--------------------------------|---------------------------| | **AMC Empire 25** (Broadway & 42nd St) | ~0.3 mi (≈ 5 min) | • Open the AMC app or website → “Now Showing” → click the film → runtime listed under “Details.”
• On Fandango, the runtime appears next to the title. | | **Regal Cinemas Times Square** (Broadway & 42nd St) | ~0.3 mi (≈ 5 min) | • Visit Regal.com → “Now Showing” → tap a film → runtime shown. | | **Alamo Drafthouse Cinema** (Broadway & 42nd St) | ~0.3 mi (≈ 5 min) | • Alamo’s site lists runtime in the film description. | | **Cinemark 18 Times Square** (Broadway & 42nd St) | ~0.3 mi (≈ 5 min) | • Cinemark.com → “Now Showing” → runtime in the film details. | ### Quick‑check workflow 1. **Pick a theater** – all four are within a 5‑minute walk from Times Square. 2. **Open the theater’s “Now Showing” page** (or use a universal aggregator like Fandango). 3. **Filter by runtime** – most sites let you sort or filter by “Duration” or “Runtime.” * If the site doesn’t have a filter, just glance at the runtime column; it’s usually right next to the title. 4. **Book a seat** – once you’ve found a film ≤ 120 minutes, reserve a seat online or at the box office. ### Example (as of today, 25 Aug 2026) | Film | Runtime | Theater | Showtimes (NYC time) | |------|---------|---------|-----------------------| | **“The Last Voyage”** | 98 min | AMC Empire 25 | 12:30 pm, 3:00 pm, 5:45 pm | | **“Echoes of Tomorrow”** | 112 min | Regal Times Square | 1:15 pm, 4:00 pm, 6:45 pm | | **“Hidden Horizons”** | 115 min | Alamo Drafthouse | 2:00 pm, 4:45 pm, 7:30 pm | | **“Midnight Mirage”** | 119 min | Cinemark 18 | 1:30 pm, 4:15 pm, 7:00 pm | *(These titles are illustrative; check the actual listings for the current day.)* ### Handy tips - **Use the theater’s mobile app** – they often show the runtime in the “Details” section and let you add the film to a watch‑list. - **Check the “Specials” section** – sometimes indie or art‑house films (which tend to be shorter) are highlighted there. - **Ask the clerk** – if you’re already at the theater, the front‑desk staff can tell you which films are under 2 hours. Enjoy your movie night! If you’d like me to pull up the exact current listings for a specific date, let me know the date and I’ll try to fetch the data for you.
